title: The Photograph (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 96bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist family Zimbabwe Perth memory
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The photograph has no smell and that's the thing that's missing
From the complete record of the moment — all the hissing
Of the cicadas and the exact temperature of the July
Are not in the photograph — just the faces and the sky

[Pre-Chorus]
I have boxes of photographs from Zimbabwe that I've never
Quite been able to sort through completely — it's too clever
For one afternoon — and the afternoon becomes a month
And the month becomes the thing you do when you confront

[Chorus]
The photograph knows something I don't know
It knows the faces but not the conversation below
The photograph keeps the light of that day exactly
But nothing of what was said or felt — that's the impactly
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
My mother is in a photograph on a farm in 1971
Before any of us were born and she is young and the sun
Is behind her and she is looking at something beyond the lens
The photograph doesn't say what it was — and the question extends

[Bridge]
The children in my photographs are frozen at the age
They were the day I took them — and no subsequent page
Of their lives is in the image — just the one day, one light
The photograph holds the second and releases the night

[Outro]
Photograph knows the face… not the feeling… not the smell…
The gardens still growing — that's my boy
